introduction.p: We will begin by considering a more familiar situation; namely, the function f(x) = x^2, which takes a real number x as an input and produces its square x^2 as its output.

statement.p: What is the value of f(3)?
Can we solve the equation f(x) = 4? If so, is the solution unique?

solution.p: If f(x)=x^2 = 4, then x = \pm2 so there is not a unique solution.

answer.p: There is not a unique solution.

statement.p: Can we solve the equation f(x) = -10? If so, is the solution unique?

solution.p: There are no solutions to the equation f(x)=x^2=-10.

statement.p: Remember that composing two functions means we use the output from one function as the input into the other; that is, (g\circ h)(x) = g(h(x)). What function results from composing (g\circ h)(x)?

solution.p: Composing the functions, we find that g(h(x)) = g(-\frac13x)= -\frac23 x. We see that the composition is a new linear function whose slope is obtained by multiplying the slopes of g and h.
